title: Isolated Downstream Validation and Single‑Repair Effects in Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study cand-003-stud-001) that isolates purely downstream deterministic validation plus a bounded single-repair intervention under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using 1,000 deterministic intents (1,000 paired episodes) drawn from a synthetic workflow stress corpus and a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; any paired outcome difference can therefore arise only from the validator decision and at most one permitted repair call (guarded arm). Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; discordants n10 = 5 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only); preregistered primary test exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). Preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.001, 0.01]. Total hosted model calls recorded = 1005 (1,000 shared initial + 5 repair). We present the exact McNemar as the confirmatory inference, the bootstrap interval as a preregistered descriptive summary, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, ceiling effects, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from operator intent to device configuration promises operational efficiency but raises safety risks: incorrect command ordering, transient invariant violations, and unauthorized touches of protected fields can convert plausible plans into damaging live changes. Empirical surveys and controlled benchmarks document hallucination and structured-output failure modes for LLMs in code- and config-like generation [1],[2]; these failure modes motivate architectures that combine generation with downstream verification, repair, and governance layers. However, when generation and validation interact (for example, independent first-pass generations or constrained decoding in one arm but not the other), attributing improvement to the downstream verifier alone is ambiguous.

This study isolates the downstream effect of a deterministic validator plus at most one permitted repair by reusing the same initial sampled candidate for baseline and guarded conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). The resulting estimand is precisely the paired difference between baseline single‑shot/initial validity and final guarded‑pipeline validity after deterministic validation and any allowed single repair. This design intentionally rules out first‑pass sampling differences as a source of paired outcome differences and therefore measures only validator/repair marginal returns. We preregistered the design, analysis, and decision rules (study id cand-003-stud-001) and executed the run with a registered analysis executor and deterministic task selection.
sections.related_work:
Prior work on LLM-driven configuration and structured-output tasks converges on three relevant points. First, LLMs exhibit syntactic and semantic errors and are sensitive to prompt and decoding choices; broad empirical surveys and targeted code/config benchmarks document hallucinations and prompt sensitivity that materially affect correctness [3],[4]. Second, multiple proposals and demonstrations pair generation with validation and repair; system and benchmark papers show that verifier-augmented pipelines can reduce observable errors in offline or synthetic settings, but the magnitude of measured gains depends on validator coverage, benchmark construction, and whether generative sampling differs between conditions [5],[6],[7]. Third, architecture and governance proposals emphasize protocol-mediated execution, auditability, and bounded tool interfaces as necessary complements to any single model’s behavior, arguing that operational reliability depends on validator fidelity and orchestration policies rather than on the generator alone [8],[9],[10].

Two lessons from the verified literature directly motivated our shared_initial_candidate paired design. Many prior generate→validate→repair evaluations combine downstream verification with independent sampling or decoding changes; this conflation complicates causal attribution of any observed improvement to the validator itself. Methodological and system papers therefore recommend isolating downstream verification effects before exploring generator+validator interventions [5],[11]. Second, constrained/schema-aware decoding demonstrably increases executable outputs in some structured domains, but those results are domain- and tooling-dependent, and transfer to multi-device NetOps with ordering and protected-field constraints is nontrivial; isolating downstream verifier effects complements constrained-decoding investigations by quantifying marginal returns attributable to validation and bounded repair alone [12],[13].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The preregistration (study cand-003-stud-001) was finalized prior to any hosted-model invocation. Core preregistered items executed without deviation include: task_count = 1,000 complete pairs; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both arms); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary confirmatory test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 for descriptive summaries.

Corpus, selection, and difficulty annotations. Tasks derive from the synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus. Selection deterministically mapped ordinal j∈[0,999] to fixed task indices producing 1,000 unique intents; each manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty annotations (levels include 'very_hard' and 'extreme'). Representative workflow patterns include failover_then_offline_reconfiguration, rolling_access_vlan_migration, safe_access_service_transfer, and composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance; these patterns encode ordering and transient invariants that the validator evaluates.

Adapter, model configuration, and validation. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the declared provider/model was gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). The recorded model_configuration shows temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes; only the guarded arm could call the repair provider, and at most one repair call was permitted per task. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) acts as a digital twin: it parses candidate command sequences, checks required command presence and ordering, enforces protected-field noninterference, evaluates workflow invariants, emits a binary safe-deploy decision, and logs structured validation_before, repair_applied, and validation_after traces.

Causal and statistical semantics. Because the initial candidate is shared for each pair, any paired outcome difference can arise only from the deterministic validator decision and at most one permitted repair call. The confirmatory hypothesis therefore concerns downstream validator/repair marginal effect only; generator-level interventions (prompt engineering, constrained decoding, independent sampling) were preregistered but not executed under shared_initial_candidate and so are outside the estimand. The preregistered primary inferential procedure is the exact two-sided McNemar test applied to complete pairs; the registered executor computed the exact p-value reported here. The paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was computed by resampling paired outcomes with replacement and reporting 2.5th/97.5th percentiles as a descriptive summary. All analysis seeds, resample counts, and implementation were executed by the registered analysis executor.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and calls. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete_pairs = 1,000; failed episodes = 0. Provider-call audit recorded hosted model call event count = 1,005 (1,000 shared initial generations and 5 repair invocations) and all deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Primary paired outcomes (preregistered). The observed paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625; by the prespecified α = 0.05 this does not reach significance.

Preregistered descriptive summary and bootstrap. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) computed by the registered executor is [0.001, 0.01]. This preregistered descriptive interval excludes zero despite the exact two‑sided p‑value being >0.05. This outcome reflects well-known discrete behavior in paired exact tests when discordant counts are extremely sparse: the null distribution concentrates mass on symmetric small counts so that an exact two‑sided p can exceed α even when resampling-based percentile intervals omit zero.

Repair mechanics and diagnostics. Exactly five validator-triggered repairs occurred. Archived validator traces and repair logs document that repaired candidates were rejected for rule-level violations (notably ordering errors in required_sequence and touches of protected interfaces) and that each rejected candidate produced a single repair provider call whose output passed the validator on revalidation. The five repairs are concentrated among tasks annotated 'very_hard' or 'extreme' with multi-step required_sequences in the synthetic corpus; archived representative manifests and traces reflect patterns such as composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance and rolling_access_vlan_migration. All repair events and their before/after validator traces are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive evidence and discrete paired inference. The preregistered confirmatory decision rule treats the exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 as the primary outcome; under the prespecified α = 0.05 we do not claim confirmatory support for a nonzero paired increase. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001,0.01]) is a prespecified descriptive summary and aids interpretation but does not override the confirmatory test. The apparent tension between a nondiscovering exact test and a CI that omits zero is a sampling-statistics artifact: with n10 = 5 and n01 = 0 the exact two‑sided null distribution places substantial mass on symmetric discordant counts yielding p = 0.0625, whereas bootstrap percentiles reflect resampled empirical variability and can exclude zero even when exact tests are nondiscovering. Reporting both outcomes is essential for transparent interpretation when discordant counts are sparse.

Ceiling effects, power mismatch, and design implications. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline≈0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15. Observed baseline = 0.995 is far higher than planned; this concentrates outcomes in the concordant success cell (n11 = 995) and leaves only five discordant pairs to inform the paired test. The practical consequence is that detecting tiny absolute gains (here 0.005) under exact paired tests requires either vastly larger paired samples or designs that increase discordant prevalence (for instance, independent first-pass generations, injected faults, or larger repair budgets). For future confirmatory studies aiming to detect sub‑percentage absolute gains, preregistration should target baseline operating regimes with appreciable failure prevalence or adopt enriched sampling/injection strategies to ensure informative discordant mass.

Failure‑mode patterns and validator scope. Archived traces indicate repaired cases shared common rule-level failure modes: ordering violations in required_sequence and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces. Repaired tasks come from complex multi-step workflows in the synthetic corpus; this is consistent with the intuition that workflow complexity and multi-device dependencies increase ordering vulnerabilities. However, only five repairs were observed, limiting inference about repair efficacy across the full failure-modality spectrum. The observed small marginal return is compatible with several nonexclusive explanations supported by the artifacts: (a) low prevalence of validator-detectable violations in the sampled corpus for the declared model+prompt; (b) generator behavior producing largely valid initial candidates under the declared model and prompt; and/or (c) validator coverage that omits some semantic error classes not captured by deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Design tradeoffs and interpretation scope. The shared_initial_candidate paired design precisely isolates downstream validator/repair marginal effects but precludes measuring generator-level interventions. This isolation is a methodological strength when the scientific question concerns validator marginal returns, but it is a design constraint when the broader operational question concerns generator+validator interactions. Follow-up experiments that were preregistered but not executed here (independent_condition_generation, sweep of repair budgets, model-family comparisons) are natural next steps to map marginal returns across the broader design space. Importantly, reported operational implications below are conditional on the synthetic corpus, declared model, and deterministic validator used in this run.

Operational implications and concretely prespecified follow-ups. Artifact-grounded evidence indicates that verifier-guided single repairs can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic NetOps workflows; measured marginal gains are small when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the repair budget is highly constrained. Concrete, preregistered follow-ups consistent with the archived plan include: (1) executing independent first-pass generation arms to measure generator+validator interactions and to increase discordant prevalence for paired inference; (2) sweeping repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per additional repair invocation; (3) injecting targeted failure modes or sampling difficulty strata to ensure informative discordant counts for confirmatory tests; and (4) expanding validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity across device families. Each follow-up should prespecify baseline failure ranges and adjust power calculations to expected operating regimes to avoid the ceiling-driven power shortfall observed here.

Threats to validity and limits. Construct validity: the safe-deploy binary reflects deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but prevent measuring first-pass generation differences. External validity: synthetic corpus and single declared model (gpt-5-mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: extreme baseline success produced sparse discordant counts and discrete p-value behavior, reducing sensitivity for very small absolute effects. These limitations were anticipated in the preregistration and are documented in the archived manifest.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1,000-task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar did not meet two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005. The preregistered confirmatory result is the exact McNemar outcome; the paired bootstrap CI and one‑sided test are reported as descriptive and exploratory respectively. Artifact-grounded evidence indicates downstream validator/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in structured NetOps workflows, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Mapping marginal returns across realistic operating regimes requires follow-ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, validator coverage, and model families with preregistered sampling and power plans aligned to the target failure prevalence.

This visualization supplements the preregistered exact McNemar confirmatory test and illustrates bootstrap sensitivity to sparse discordant counts.

disclosure_statement: Declared model and provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator/digital twin. Preregistration: study cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls and recorded in the archived execution manifest). Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Human role and autonomy boundary: after the autonomy lock the research run executed the preregistered experiment, analysis, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
